example.question: Under the Terms and Conditions of Belfius Bank's EUR 25 billion EMTN Programme, if the Final Terms of a Note specify 'Amortised Face Amount' and the Note becomes immediately repayable after an Event of Default, how is the amount payable determined, and which event gives a Noteholder the right to demand that immediate repayment?
example.reference_answer: The 'Event of Default Redemption Amount' is, where 'Amortised Face Amount' is specified in the Final Terms, 'an amount calculated in accordance with Condition 3(b)' (Condition 3(b)(i)(B) applies this to Notes specifying 'Amortised Face Amount' upon becoming due and payable under Condition 11). Under Condition 3(b)(ii) the Amortised Face Amount is the scheduled Zero Coupon Note Redemption Amount of the Note on the Maturity Date discounted at a rate per annum equal to the Amortisation Yield, compounded annually (for a period of less than one year, the Day Count Fraction in the Final Terms applies). Under Condition 11 this amount is payable together (if applicable) with accrued interest to the date of payment. The event giving a holder the right to give written notice to the Paying Agent that its Notes are immediately repayable is a dissolution or liquidation of the Issuer under Belgian law (bankruptcy, judicial liquidation or voluntary liquidation, other than a voluntary liquidation in connection with a reconstruction, merger or amalgamation where the continuing corporation assumes all liabilities). A payment default continuing 30 days or more only allows a holder to institute proceedings for dissolution or liquidation of the Issuer in Belgium, and a resolution action by the Relevant Resolution Authority does not entitle holders to accelerate.

repayable, whereupon the Event of Default Redemption Amount of such Note(s) together (if applicable) with… accrued interest to the date of payment shall become immediately due and payable.… shall not entitle the holders of the relevant Notes to accelerate the Issuer’s payment obligations thereunder.… “Amortised Face Amount” is specified in the applicable Final Terms, an amount calculated in accordance with… Condition 3(b) above.

(ii)    Subject to sub-paragraph (iii) below, the “Amortised Face Amount” of any such Note shall be… the scheduled Zero Coupon Note Redemption Amount of such Note on the Maturity Date discounted at a rate per annum (expressed as a percentage) equal to the Amortisation Yield… compounded annually.… Where such calculation is to be made for a period of less than one year, it shall be made on the… basis of the Day Count Fraction set out in the applicable Final Terms.

example.question: Belfius Bank's EMTN Base Prospectus says its consolidated CET1 ratio rose between end-2024 and end-2025. In the CET1 solvency-ratio commentary of Belfius's 2025 Pillar 3 report, does the headline year-on-year comparison show the same direction of change, and if not, what reference point and regulatory basis for end-2024 explain the difference?
example.reference_answer: No, not in the Pillar 3 headline comparison. Both documents give a CET1 ratio of 15.87% at 31 December 2025. The prospectus compares it with the published end-2024 ratio of 15.38% and reports an increase of +49 bps (lower total risk exposure amount, EUR -3.0 billion to EUR 72.1 billion, partly offset by lower CET1 capital, EUR -111 million). The Pillar 3 report compares it with the pro forma end-2024 ratio under CRR 3/CRD 6 (Basel IV) and reports a decrease of 29 bps (lower prudential capital -15 bps, higher risk exposures -14 bps). It also notes that the published and reported end-2024 ratio under CRR 2/CRD 5 was 15.38% (slightly adjusted from 15.39% after a late Corep correction), against which the ratio rose; the transition to Basel IV added 78 bps to the 2024 ratio (pro forma 16.16%). So the difference is the 2024 reference point: published CRR 2/CRD 5 basis (15.38%, +49 bps) versus pro forma CRR 3/CRD 6 basis (about 16.16%, -29 bps); +49 bps and -29 bps differ by 78 bps.

example.question: Under the definitions in the consolidated Prospectus for Germany of Guggenheim Global Investments plc dated 9 November 2023 (which consolidates the Company's prospectus dated 4 September 2023), could the Directors of Guggenheim Global Investments plc set up a Fund that has only one Dealing Day in a calendar month? Explain what a Dealing Day is and where the term 'Business Day' on which it is based is specified.
example.reference_answer: No. A 'Dealing Day' is defined, for each Fund, as each Business Day on which subscriptions for, redemptions of and exchanges of relevant Shares can be made by the Company, as specified in the Supplement for the relevant Fund and/or such other Dealing Days as the Directors determine and notify to Shareholders in advance, provided that there are at least two Dealing Days in each month occurring at regular intervals. 'Business Day' is not defined in the Prospectus itself: it means, in relation to any Fund, each day specified as such in the Supplement for the relevant Fund. So at least two Dealing Days per month, at regular intervals, are required.
